title: Private VPC capacity checker and BOM worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a working worksheet to estimate GPU fleet sizing, regional distribution, utilization targets, and a rough BOM for Private / VPC deployments for mid-market and enterprise customers. Use this when scoping initial infra requirements for a customer who wants a dedicated VPC cluster (single-region or multi-region).

TL;DR (quick answers):
- Target production QPS profile: 120 sustained inference requests per minute with 75% peaked burst headroom.
- Preferred GPU types (per-customer): H100 for high-throughput/latency-critical; A100 80GB for mixed workloads.
- Initial recommended cluster: 8 x H100-80GB per region (2 racks) for moderate enterprise load; single-region BOM estimate ~ $1.1M CAPEX + 18% network+ops.
- Utilization planning: aim for 45–65% token-throughput utilization to allow steady-state autoscaling and headroom for cache/memory spikes.

Assumptions (configurable inputs):
- Average tokens per request: 300 tokens (prompt + response).
- Average tokens per second processed per GPU (H100): ~1800 tokens/s (aggregated, after batching).
- Hourly traffic profile: base 60% of peak for 75% of time, peak window 25% of time.
- Service SLO: P95 latency < 250ms for streaming short responses, P99 graceful degrade.
- Redundancy: N+1 cluster redundancy for rack failure.
- Network egress inside VPC ignored for billing; cross-region egress estimated separately.

Workload profiles (examples):
1) Chat-heavy enterprise: long context (8k tokens), low qps but high per-request tokens -> prefer more memory per GPU (A100 80GB).
2) Low-latency embedder: many small requests (<=64 tokens) -> prefer more modest GPUs with more concurrent contexts (L4 or A10X).
3) Mixed: 30% long-form, 70% short; use heterogeneous routing across GPU pools.

Sizing steps (manual):
1) Calculate token/sec demand = requests_per_sec * avg_tokens_per_request.
2) Pick GPU type and per-GPU token/s estimate.
3) Required GPUs = ceil(token/sec_demand / per_gpu_tokens_sec / desired_utilization).
4) Convert GPUs to servers (gpus_per_server depends on SKU, e.g., 8x H100 per server typical).
5) Add redundancy + management nodes + load-balancers + storage nodes.

Sample calculation (single-region):
- Target steady RPS: 2 requests/sec (120 per minute) average -> requests_per_sec = 2.0
- Avg tokens/request = 300 -> token/sec demand = 600 tokens/s
- Use H100 per-GPU throughput (conservative) = 1800 tokens/s
- Desired utilization = 0.55 (55%) -> effective per-GPU capacity = 1800 * 0.55 = 990 tokens/s
- GPUs required = ceil(600 / 990) = 1 GPU -> but account for burst and redundancy -> plan for 4 GPUs (1 production scale + N+1 across racks)
- If we standardize on 8x GPU servers -> we would provision one 8-GPU server (w/ autoscale) or split across racks: 4 GPUs requires 1 server, but for redundancy we prefer 2 servers (4 GPUs each) -> 2 servers total.

BOM rough table (single-region example, two-server redundant build):
- 2 x Rack-mounted servers (8x H100 each) – vendor list price per server $350k -> 700k
- 16 x H100 GPUs (included in server price above in this quoting approach) -> aggregated cost captured in server unit pricing
- 2 x Top-of-Rack switches (100Gbps) – $18k each -> 36k
- 1 x Aggregation switch / L4 load balancer appliance -> 45k
- 1 x 10Gbps transit for on-prem management (firewalls, VPN appliances) -> 12k
- Power distribution units + rack PDUs (2 racks) -> 6k
- Rack enclosures (2) -> 8k
- Storage: 2 x NVMe 3.2TB per server for model cache + 3 x NFS backup nodes -> 30k
- KMS / HSM integration (one-time config) -> 15k
- Installation & cabling services (onsite) -> 22k
- Contingency (spares, extra NICs, accessories) -> 20k
- Estimated subtotal CAPEX (hardware) -> $894k
- Professional services + first-year support (20%) -> $178.8k
- Estimated total first-year cost -> $1.0728M (round to $1.08M)

Notes on BOM: vendor discounts vary; for enterprise deals we typically negotiate 10–25% off list. For hosted-like deployments where Redwood provides dedicated capacity we may convert to OPEX model.

Region distribution guidance:
- Multi-region required for geo-SLA or data residency: replicate minimal cluster in each region, keep heavy training/cache primaries in the customer-preferred region.
- Cross-region active/active only if customer accepts extra egress costs; otherwise active/passive with failover.

Network and power planning highlights:
- 100 Gbps per rack recommended for H100 clusters, with 200 Gbps if inter-node KV cache routing latency is critical.
- Provision for 30–40 kW per rack for fully populated 8xH100 nodes; validate datacenter PDUs and HVAC capacity.
- PDU redundancy: A/B power feeds recommended.

Utilization targets and monitoring:
- Slack headroom intentionally maintained (target 45–65% average GPU utilization). This reduces tail latency and preserves KV cache effectiveness.
- Metrics to track: per-GPU token/sec, batch size distribution, idle time, queue latency, P50/P95/P99 token latency, cold-start rate for model loads.

Capacity-run checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm customer peak RPS and 95th percentile token size
- [ ] Confirm preferred GPU SKUs and vendor preference (NVIDIA/Hyperscaler SKUs)
- [ ] Verify rack power/power feeds and HVAC limits
- [ ] Confirm network uplink and cross-region bandwidth budget
- [ ] Decide replication strategy (active/active vs active/passive)
- [ ] Allocate management and monitoring nodes (Prometheus, tracing, S3 gateway)
- [ ] Schedule onsite install window and procurement lead times (GPUs often 8–16 weeks)

Risks and mitigations:
- Lead times for GPUs: plan 12–20 week procurement lead time for H100 in constrained markets; mitigate by starting procurement early and offering a staged rollout using A100 fallback.
- Underestimated batch characteristics: run at least 48-hour traffic replay using customer traces to validate per-GPU throughput claims.
- Power/cooling mismatch: require datacenter power audit; budget for HVAC upgrades if necessary.

Appendix A — Quick reference server SKU mapping (internal):
- SKU-H100-8U: 8x H100-80GB, dual-socket host, 2x 2TB NVMe, 2x 100Gbps NICs, redundant PSUs (vendor example price: $350k list)
- SKU-A100-4U: 4x A100-80GB, single-socket host, 1x 2TB NVMe, 2x 100Gbps NICs (vendor example price: $220k list)
- SKU-L4-1U: 2x L4 GPUs for edge-like deployments (price: $35k list)

Appendix B — Quick formulas (paste into a sheet):
- requests_per_sec = round(desired_rpm / 60, 3)
- token_sec_demand = requests_per_sec * avg_tokens_per_request
- per_gpu_effective = per_gpu_tokens_raw * target_utilization
- gpus_needed = ceil(token_sec_demand / per_gpu_effective)
- servers_needed = ceil(gpus_needed / gpus_per_server)

Next steps / owner actions:
- Aisha to run a customer trace replay for ACME Corp (JIRA-DEPLOY-4589) and produce a 72-hour throughput simulation by 2025-03-10.
- Jamal to contact vendor reps for three quotes (HPE, Supermicro, Dell) and capture EDD/lead times by 2025-03-20.
- Priya to validate power & network on customer site with a datacenter audit (template attached reference CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-1203).

Open questions (to resolve):
- Should we support on-prem KMS or require cloud-managed HSM for this customer? (security team input required)
- Acceptable RPO for model cache persistence during failover?

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Keep this worksheet lean; convert into a proper Google Sheet after the replay run so we can hook formulas into the telemetry export.
- Consider building a small CLI tool to generate these BOM estimates from a 5-field customer input form.

Revision log:
- 2024-08-15: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-09-02: added rough BOM line items + vendor price estimates (Jamal)

End of doc.
